methodological_rigor.justification: This single-institution retrospective cohort study of 25 patients with liver-limited metastatic anal SCCA uses appropriate Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and univariate Cox proportional hazards models. The cohort is well-characterized with detailed clinicopathologic data. However, the small sample size (n=25) severely limits statistical power; multivariate analysis was not performed and only one factor (poor differentiation) reached significance on univariate analysis. Selection bias is substantial and explicitly acknowledged—all patients had disease control on systemic therapy prior to liver-directed therapy. The 30-year study period encompasses major treatment advances.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a retrospective single-institution case series (LoE 4) addressing a rare and poorly characterized clinical scenario—liver-limited metastatic SCCA. The reported median OS of 51.3 months substantially exceeds historical systemic therapy data (20-29 months) and prior multi-institutional series, providing clinically meaningful preliminary evidence for liver-directed therapy in selected patients. The rarity of this condition means even small series contribute meaningfully to the evidence base, and the findings will directly inform multidisciplinary tumor board discussions.

reporting_quality.justification: The study follows observational reporting conventions with clear eligibility criteria, data collection procedures, and survival analyses with confidence intervals. The comprehensive introduction includes current treatment landscape through InterAACT-2/retifanlimab FDA approval (2025), reflecting contemporaneous reporting. Limitations are transparently acknowledged including selection bias and inability to perform multivariate analysis. No public data deposit is mentioned, and specific chemotherapy regimen details are incompletely captured for some patients.

novelty_literature.justification: This study provides one of the larger single-institution experiences for liver-directed therapy in metastatic SCCA, with more contemporary systemic therapy integration than prior series by Pawlik et al. and Rogers et al. The discussion of ctDNA as an emerging biomarker for MRD detection in SCCA adds novel clinical context. However, the core observation—that selected patients with liver-limited SCCA benefit from metastasectomy—has been previously reported, making this primarily a confirmatory contribution with extended follow-up.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized and clearly written, with a particularly comprehensive and up-to-date introduction covering the evolving systemic therapy landscape through 2025 (retifanlimab FDA approval). Survival analyses are clearly presented with confidence intervals. Limitations are explicitly and specifically enumerated. The emerging ctDNA section adds clinical depth. The discussion is appropriately cautious given the small sample size and explicit about selection bias.

key_strengths: One of the larger single-institution series for liver-directed therapy in this rare disease over 30 years at a major academic center
Comprehensive and current treatment landscape introduction including 2025 retifanlimab FDA approval data from InterAACT-2/POD1UM-303
Excellent rule-out of extrahepatic disease as eligibility criterion, ensuring a homogeneous and clinically relevant comparison group
Transparent acknowledgment of selection bias and limitations with appropriate statistical caveats for all subgroup findings
key_concerns: Very small cohort (n=25) with only 22 months median follow-up severely underpowers the study and precludes multivariate analysis; wide confidence intervals throughout
Substantial selection bias toward favorable biology (all patients had disease control prior to liver-directed therapy); true population-level benefit cannot be estimated
30-year study period encompasses fundamental changes in systemic therapy (pre-immunotherapy to retifanlimab era), making temporal heterogeneity a major confounder
No public data deposit; detailed systemic therapy regimens not systematically captured for all patients
chief_reviewer.rationale: This well-written case series from the Mayo Clinic provides the best available evidence for liver-directed therapy in the rare setting of liver-limited SCCA metastases, with a median OS (51.3 months) substantially exceeding historical systemic therapy benchmarks; Tier 3 acceptance is appropriate with minor revisions to address temporal heterogeneity in the 30-year cohort.
